note: First verdict 2026-11-20 by an independent agent. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1.1: "Note that the Local and Remote ports may not be available in the case of receipt of a fragmented packet or if the port fields have been protected by IPsec (encrypted); thus, a value of OPAQUE also MUST be supported." No tag, and none is owed until the code exists: the {gap} is true at the producers. Ze parses OPAQUE (traffic_selector.go PortSelectorFromWire reads the 65535/0 pair, parsePortSelector accepts `opaque` on a peer traffic selector) but programs it nowhere: PortSelector.ProgrammableForProtocol answers false for PortOpaque, checkPortProgrammable refuses it at commit with an operator error, and parseSPDPort refuses it in an operator SPD entry. So an operator cannot write an OPAQUE selector that takes effect, which is the missing behavior, owed by plan/post-release/features/spec-ipsec-opaque-selector-port-mask.md. The annotation's ICMP part is also accurate at the producers: ICMPSelector.MatchesFragmentTypeCode, SPDPolicy.validateICMPFragments refusing an out or both entry holding type 0 code 0, and spdEntryHasTransit projecting no forward entry for one, covered only by untagged unit tests, with the packet proof owned by AC-9 of plan/release/validation/spec-ipsec-fragment-receive-and-kernel-proof.md. Scope finding for that AC: this row's sentence names only the Local and Remote ports; the ICMP type and code bullet of Section 4.4.1.1 says only "Note that the ICMP message type and code may not be available in the case of receipt of a fragmented packet", with no keyword. AC-9's packet tests can therefore prove at most an ICMP case of this row, carried as {partial}: they cannot lift the OPAQUE port gap, and a tag that cites them for the whole row would over-claim.
